newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Uralsvyazinform says can issue for ADRs.
newsitem.headline: Russia Uralsvyazinform says can issue for ADRs.

text.p: Russian regional telecom Uralsvyazinform has received permission from the U.S. Securities and Exchanges Commission to issue level-one American Depositary Receipts, a senior company official said on Tuesday.
"For now we will try to place them in the United States," said first deputy chief executive Alexander Vokhmin. "There are already a lot of shares in communications companies being offered in Europe."
A company securities spokesman said one ADR covers 200 ordinary shares with a face value of 100 roubles. The ADR programme could cover up to 42 percent of shares.
The Bank of New York is acting as the depositary for the placement. Clifford Chance is the legal consultant.
Level one ADRs are share receipts issued on existing shares to allow trade abroad, including in the U.S. They do not raise new capital.
Vokhmin said the company hoped to sell up to 10 percent of its shares to Western investors in October in a separate deal which he said was still being worked out.
He added the stake would be consolidated from shares currently held by the company and existing shareholders. He said no new shares would be issued for the sale.
"It will not be just our shares, it will be a consolidated stake," he said, adding the company hoped to bring Russian investment bank Brunswick on board as its agent.
Holding company Svyazinvest holds a controlling 51 percent stake in Uralsvyazinform.
